assertions.name: AI-36 real React/HTTP confirmation lifecycle with synthetic transport revises a dependent contact, confirms the displayed immutable revision and resumes only after showing the committed supplier receipt
AI-36 real React/HTTP confirmation lifecycle with synthetic transport reconciles a malformed successful confirmation response through GETs without issuing a second write (es)
AI-36 real React/HTTP confirmation lifecycle with synthetic transport reconciles a malformed successful confirmation response through GETs without issuing a second write (en)
AI-36 real React/HTTP confirmation lifecycle with synthetic transport retires a previous session's pending confirmation and denies its private proposal without adopting its late receipt
AI-36 real React/HTTP confirmation lifecycle with synthetic transport removes an observed partial execution's receipts after access revocation and prevents resuming from stale authority

scenarios.behavior: Registered dependent-contact correction creates revision2; no confirm until button; double click yields one challenge and one confirmation for exact revision/hash; challenge absent from query cache; partial supplier receipt remains; explicit resume sends current execution CAS and shows both receipts
scenarios.boundary: Frontend one-request guard and request identity only, not SQL atomicity or backend idempotence

scenarios.behavior: HTTP200 invalid confirmation payload is rejected by production schema, blocks duplicate confirm, then GET current proposal+execution recovers committed partial result without another write
scenarios.boundary: Controlled malformed adapter response; no real provider or uncertain SQL commit induced

scenarios.behavior: Actor/session changes during pending confirmation; new scope denied; old private proposal removed and late successful receipt ignored with no operation GET or cross-session cache adoption
scenarios.boundary: Frontend session race only; server authorization tested separately

scenarios.behavior: Execution observed with partial receipt then GET403; receipt and resume controls removed; no resume mutation; one error toast
scenarios.boundary: Synthetic access denial; does not claim server revocation enforcement

scope_limits: Does not independently close every NR scenario or certify production acceptance
Provider availability, SQL atomicity/idempotence, storage retention and runtime fencing require their own real integration evidence
Existing page routing/attachments/compaction/read-only/history tests remain part of final module/full-client regression

limitations: Coverage measures instrumented code reachability rather than semantic or end-to-end product acceptance
No new skips, TODOs, ignore directives, exclusions or production changes introduced
Includes isolated existing unit/component fixtures alongside the new cross-component acceptance tests
